what: Issue #92 acceptance-condition-4 diagnostic profiling of the Newton-Schulz block circular-buffer windows
scope_note: This record must not be used as a throughput headline or to replace any prior throughput, correctness, or error record.

multipass_passes: fpu, pack, unpack, l1_1, instrn (L1 bank 1)
limitations: Counters are a one-window diagnostic only.
The official all-group mode replayed the workload in two L1-bank passes; these are not throughput samples.

noc.interpretation_note: NoC counts identify reader reads and writer writes; overlap with RISC intervals is not treated as causal proof.

interpretation.evidence_level: sufficient to identify compute-side remaining bottleneck candidates; insufficient for exclusive phase causality

evidence: NCRISC reader and BRISC writer spend most of their time waiting for compute: in the two-window case NCRISC CB-empty wait is 79.173% and BRISC CB/output wait is 96.829%. These are producer/consumer waits because compute has not consumed or returned the buffers, not evidence that data movement blocks compute.

The one-window-to-two-window whole-kernel intervals fall from NCRISC 995419 to 808594 cycles, BRISC 1044103 to 895937 cycles, and TRISC0-2 approximately 1037570-1038311 to 888885-889611 cycles; the full interval is approximately 15% shorter.

The recorded NoC volume is 118116352 bytes read plus 67108864 bytes written per launch. Using the recorded approximately 0.774 ms launch interval, this derives 185225216 / 0.000774 seconds = approximately 239-240 GB/s aggregate decimal bandwidth, or approximately 2.17-2.18 GB/s per 110 cores (rounded to approximately 240 GB/s and 2 GB/s/core). This is a derived diagnostic estimate, not a new measurement.
The one-window NoC trace shows the expected external reader and writer transfers, while the two-window change preserves the same block operation configuration.

One-window stored counters report math/FPU utilization of about 36% from math_util_median_range 35.63862970599092-35.67909072287391%, math-thread idle wait of about 0.51% from math_idle_wait_avg_range 0.5110193992008973-0.5117562753970224%, unpack-thread instruction availability of about 22% from instruction_available_avg_ranges.unpack_t0 22.23482101729926-22.273140109756465%, and pack-thread stall of about 56% from thread_stall_avg_ranges.pack_thread_t2 56.37487928142017-56.56814068139432%.

The low FPU utilization is not explained by a large math-thread waiting-for-unpack fraction. TRISC instruction supply and unpack/math/pack handoff, especially pack-side stall, are the main remaining bottleneck candidates.
TRISC named wait/active sections are zero and the TRISC body is unclassified by the L1 cycle-counter pages; exact kernel phase attribution requires kernel-internal zones.
Two-buffer performance counters are unavailable, so this candidate interpretation has no mode-to-mode counter comparison.

interpretation.conclusion: Two-buffering removed/shortened the block-boundary I/O and compute serialization (the full interval is approximately 15% shorter). The remaining bottleneck is on the compute side, not data movement (NoC and DRAM/L1 reads/writes). Within compute, FPU utilization remains about 36%; TRISC instruction supply and unpack/math/pack handoff, especially pack-side stall, are the main candidates. Exact kernel phase attribution requires kernel-internal zones. This is not an exclusive causal claim because the compute body remains unclassified and two-buffer performance counters are unavailable.

limitations: The main profiler runs used TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER=1 with Watcher explicitly unset; no Watcher-plus-profiler evidence is claimed.
The prior Watcher-plus-profiler attempt failed before kernel launch with BRISC ELF segment overflow; the prior power-off PCIe read-0xffffffff incident is preserved as operational history.

The repository device-profile parser expects an older tt-metal CSV header; the current pinned image emits zone name/type/run host ID fields, so whole-kernel intervals were decoded with an offline compatibility parser without rerunning the successful profiles.

The first official counter-tool setup attempt failed before kernel launch because its default watcher log path was under the read-only source mount; the bounded multipass run completed after setting TT_METAL_LOGS_PATH to the writable diagnostic output mount.
The main profiles have one timed sample each and are diagnostic only; no p50/p99/p99.9 or throughput headline is derived here.
No source-zone change was required; reader and writer profile sources provide built-in whole-kernel intervals, and compute provides NS-COMPUTE-TOTAL.
